description: Regroup an asset's versions, as the version menu and drag-and-drop do in the Flask app; no media or feedback is ever deleted. action=add: make other assets or versions the NEWEST versions of asset_id (the asset that keeps its title, link and sharing). A source asset id brings ALL its versions, and that source asset then stops existing: its title and link go, and its versions take asset_id's sharing. A version id moves just that version (if it was its asset's only version, that asset goes the same way). Sources are added in order; the last becomes the current version. Use this when a revision was uploaded as a separate asset. Refused when a source is still uploading, is in another team, or is shared more narrowly than asset_id (sharing is changed in the app). action=split: move each version in version_ids into its own new asset in the same folder, named after the version, with the same sharing. An asset always keeps at least one version; a version that is already alone is reported already_separate. action=reorder: order lists every version id of asset_id exactly once, top first. The top version becomes the current one (what the asset link opens), and version numbers follow the order. Feedback always stays on its version. contents(asset_id) lists an asset's versions. To add NEW media as a version, use the upload tools with version_of. Results are per item; earlier items are not undone if a later one fails.

asset_id.description: The asset (any of its ids). Required for add and reorder.

order.description: reorder: every version id of the asset, top first

source_ids.description: add: asset or version ids to add, in order

version_ids.description: split: version ids to split out

name: versions_update
title: Add, split or reorder an asset's versions
